title: Docs/README: unify tool-calling terminology + link canonical examples
author: Dana Lo
release_notes: Docs-only: standardize on “tool calling” (not “function calling”) in TS SDK docs/README; replace legacy snippets with links to canonical examples in redwood-examples; clarify structured output terminology and failure modes.
body:
Title: Docs/README: unify tool-calling terminology + link canonical examples

Context
We’re seeing drift across docs/examples where the TS SDK alternates between “function calling” and “tool calling”, and some README snippets still point to legacy event shapes. This PR is a docs/README cleanup pass to align TS wording with the canonical terminology approved in PM-612 and to point users at the single source of truth in redwood-examples.

Motivation / user impact
- Reduce confusion: users search for “tool calling” in the docs site and don’t find the TS README sections.
- Reduce support load: old snippets encourage parsing tool args mid-stream, leading to partial JSON parse errors (see SUP-18433).
- Keep parity with refreshed examples landing in redwood-examples (PR #145) and the streaming/tooling refresh work in ENG-2844.

What changed
- README terminology:
  - “Function calling” -> “Tool calling” (primary term)
  - “Functions” -> “Tools” in headings, prose, and code comments
  - Keep a short note: “Tool calling (also known as function calling)” once, for discoverability.
- Link out to canonical, runnable examples:
  - Replace inline multi-page snippets with links to redwood-examples canonical TS examples for:
    - Streaming token deltas
    - Tool calling (single + parallel)
    - Structured output (schema validation + retry)
- Structured output wording:
  - Prefer “structured output” over “JSON mode” in TS docs.
  - Add a small callout that validation should happen after finalization (do not attempt to parse tool args on every delta).
- Minor hygiene:
  - Fix a couple of outdated parameter names in docs blocks.
  - Update internal cross-links within the README so anchors don’t break after heading renames.

Non-goals
- No SDK API changes.
- No changes to runtime behavior or event payloads.
- No new examples added here (canonical set lives in redwood-examples).

Notes on “tools vs functions”
We standardize on:
- User-facing: “tools”, “tool calling”, “tool call”.
- Protocol objects: the wire field is still tool_calls; we do not mention “functions” unless in the one-time parenthetical.

Docs snippet guidance added
- Don’t parse tool call args until the model indicates the tool call is complete.
- Treat partial tool args as expected during streaming; only finalize/validate after full aggregation.

Illustrative snippet (README excerpt)
Before:
- “Function calling allows you to…”
- Inline example attempted JSON.parse on every tool delta

After:
- “Tool calling allows you to…”
- Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples/tree/main/typescript/tools
- Callout: “Aggregate tool call argument deltas and parse once complete.”

Checklist
- [x] Terminology matches PM-612 (tools / structured output)
- [x] Removed/updated legacy snippets that referenced older streaming events
- [x] Links point to canonical redwood-examples locations
- [x] Security callout: examples assume allowlisted tool dispatch (no arbitrary execution)

Related
- ENG-2844 (TS SDK examples refresh)
- PM-612 (terminology alignment)
- redwood-examples PR #145 (canonical examples)
- SUP-18433 (schema mismatch from older snippet; resolved by pointing to canonical examples)

Screenshots
N/A (README-only).

docs(readme): replace legacy inline snippets with canonical example links
docs(structured-output): clarify validation timing + retry note
chore(docs): fix anchors and minor typos

docs/streaming.md (terminology pass + remove legacy snippet reference)
docs/troubleshooting.md (add short note pointing to canonical examples for parsing patterns)
conversation:
Ibrahim Khan (review): Please make sure we only include the “also known as function calling” parenthetical once, otherwise we’ll regress back into mixed terms. Also: can you add a short line warning against parsing tool args per-delta? That’s the #1 TS support issue.

Dana Lo (author): Done. Kept the parenthetical only in the first mention under Tool calling, and added a callout box in the tools/streaming section about aggregating deltas and parsing once complete.

Elliot Price (review): Link targets look good, but can we make them stable? Prefer linking to the folder path (not a specific file) since we may rename filenames during snippet-test rollout.

Dana Lo (author): Updated links to the folder paths under redwood-examples/typescript/{streaming,tools,structured-output}.

Henry Cho (review): Wording request: please use “structured output” consistently and avoid “JSON mode” except where we explicitly call it out as legacy terminology.

Dana Lo (author): Updated. “JSON mode” appears once in parentheses as legacy wording.

Marcus Lin (security review): Thanks for removing the inline snippet that looked like it executed arbitrary tool names. Please add one sentence: “Only dispatch tools from an allowlist.”

Dana Lo (author): Added in Tool calling section.

Ibrahim Khan (final): LGTM once CI is green.

Elliot Price (final): Approved.

Merge: Squash merge.
